answers.answer: Reveal a shuffled region card and place the King there. Each player takes another region card as their home region and places their Grande there. Each player’s ten Caballeros are split as two in their home region beside the Grande, one on the first success-track space, and seven in their court.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘reveal the top card and put the King in that region’; the next card determines home. Ten Caballeros: two home, one on the first success-track space, seven in court.

answers.answer: In round 1, players choose who begins playing power cards. In later rounds, the player who took the last turn in the preceding round begins. Others play clockwise. A power-card value already played that round may not be matched.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 2: ‘Players choose who begins’ in round 1; later the preceding round’s last-turn player begins; others play clockwise; no value already played this round may be matched.

answers.answer: Turns are taken in descending power-card value. At the start of your turn, recruit up to the number shown on your power card from the provinces into your court; recruiting fewer is allowed. Recruitment happens before choosing an action card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 3–4: ‘Take turns in descending power-card value’; ‘At the start of your turn recruit up to’ the allowance; ‘After recruitment, choose’ an action card.

answers.answer: If your provinces do not have enough of your Caballeros, you may take your own from the board to make up the difference. The King’s region and Castillo cannot supply pieces for recruitment.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 3: ‘you may take your own from the board to make up the difference’; the King’s region is taboo and the Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.

answers.answer: Ordinary deployment moves Caballeros from your court to regions adjacent to the King’s current region and/or to the Castillo, dividing the allowance among destinations as desired. It may be split across those destinations, and the printed number is a maximum, so you may deploy fewer or none.
answers.evidence: Actions: deployment is ‘a maximum’; may deploy fewer, including none; move from court to any regions adjacent to the King and/or Castillo, ‘dividing the allowance freely.’

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary deployment and the special action may be done in either order. Each must be completed before beginning the other; neither may be split or interleaved. The special action may be declined.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 4: do them ‘in either order,’ complete one before starting the other, ‘neither may be split or interleaved’; may decline the special action.

answers.answer: After a player’s turn, their selected action card is laid aside and later players cannot choose it. At the end of the round, discard any face-up action cards left unselected. The King card is revealed again every round and is never permanently discarded.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 5: selected card is laid aside; remaining face-up cards are discarded after all turns; the King card ‘is revealed again every round and never permanently discarded.’

answers.answer: The King’s region is taboo: Caballeros, Grandes, and mobile scoreboards cannot move into or out of it, and special actions do not override this restriction. It may still be scored. Moving the King changes which region is protected.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: ‘no Caballero, Grande or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of’ the King’s region; it may still be scored; actions that move the King change the protected region.

answers.answer: Clearly announce how many Caballeros you put into the Castillo. The King’s location does not restrict entry; any or all Caballeros being added or moved may go there. They cannot be removed by an action and leave only during general scoring.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: ‘any or all may go into the Castillo, regardless of the King’s location. Announce clearly how many’; no action removes them; they leave only during general scoring.

answers.answer: General scoring occurs after rounds 3, 6, and 9. In order: (1) each player secretly selects one destination region other than the King’s region for all of their Castillo Caballeros, placing the disk face down; (2) uncover and score the Castillo; (3) reveal disks and move all Castillo Caballeros to their owners’ selected destinations; (4) score the nine regions in scoring-track order. Destinations are chosen before uncovering the Castillo.
answers.evidence: General scoring stages: after rounds 3, 6, 9; ‘Secretly select destinations before uncovering the Castillo’; then score Castillo, reveal disks and empty it, then score nine regions in track order.

answers.answer: A player may not split their Castillo Caballeros: they all go to one destination. The selected destination is normally any board region except the King’s region, and the pieces cannot be kept in the Castillo. If a player selects the King’s region, their Castillo pieces go to their court instead.
answers.evidence: General scoring: each player’s Castillo Caballeros ‘must go to one region’; destination is any board region except the King’s region; if someone selected the King’s region, their pieces go to court; replace the Castillo empty.

answers.answer: The three players tied for first each score 3 (the second-place value); the player with three Caballeros scores 1 (third-place value). Grandes do not count toward majority; only Caballeros count.
answers.evidence: The 5/3/1 example with counts 4,4,4,3 scores 3,3,3,1. Region ranks: ‘Only Caballeros count’; a Grande contributes zero Caballeros.

answers.answer: The players with counts 4, 3, 2, and 2 score 6, 4, 0, and 0, respectively.
answers.evidence: Publisher example: on 6/4/2, counts 4,3,2,2 score 6,4,0,0.

answers.answer: In a two-player game, only first place can pay; in a three-player game, first and second can pay. A two-player tie for first shifts to second-place value, then the player-count cutoff applies, so neither player scores.
answers.evidence: Region ranks: ‘Two players: only first place can pay. Three players: only first and second can pay.’ A two-player tie for first pays neither after the rank shift and cutoff.

answers.answer: Whenever the relevant region is scored, including in a special scoring, award +2 for the sole majority holder in the King’s region and +2 when the sole majority holder has their own Grande in that region. Neither bonus is awarded on a tie for first.
answers.evidence: Bonuses apply whenever the region is scored, including special scorings: King’s bonus +2 for sole majority holder in the King’s region; home bonus +2 for sole majority holder with their own Grande there; neither on a tie for first.

answers.answer: No. Special scoring uncovers and scores the Castillo, then covers the same Caballeros again. It does not redistribute or empty them; redistribution waits until general scoring.
answers.evidence: Stack 3: ‘Uncover and score it, then put the Castillo over the same Caballeros’; redistribution waits until general scoring.

answers.answer: A mobile scoreboard may be placed at the Castillo. It may not move into or out of the King’s region, and the two scoreboards may not be stacked on each other. They must be right side up as 8/4/0 or 4/0/0; they cannot be rotated to invent other values.
answers.evidence: Stack 4: Castillo is allowed; no movement into or out of King’s region; scoreboards cannot be stacked; place right side up as 8/4/0 or 4/0/0, never reversed or rotated.

answers.answer: You may move your Grande to another region except the King’s region or Castillo, but it cannot leave the King’s region. The destination may already contain several Grandes. After moving it, the destination becomes your new home region.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Grande: move to another region except King’s region or Castillo; it cannot leave the King’s region; destination may already contain several Grandes; destination becomes your new home region.

answers.answer: The recovery action returns any one of your played power cards to your hand, including the card played this turn. You need not reveal which card you choose, though taking the visible top card is apparent.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Power Cards: return ‘any one’ played power card, including this turn’s; ‘You need not reveal which’; taking the visible top card is apparent.

answers.answer: The standard game ends after all stages of the third general scoring, after round 9. The player furthest along the success track wins. The summary gives no additional endgame tiebreaker.
answers.evidence: End: finish all stages of the third general scoring after round 9; whoever is furthest along the success track wins; no additional endgame tiebreaker is given.
